title: 第 15章 弟子知错第 16章 修行人的规矩
slug: 杀妖涨修为道爷我成了
lines: 水滴答滴答落在脚边，在青石板上洇开一小片深色。
磨刀。
师父在磨刀。
沈回低头看了看自己这双昨天刚放完火的手，又抬头望了望天。
日头挺好，风也挺和煦，院角那棵老槐树上还落着两只麻雀，叽叽喳喳叫得正欢。
一切都挺好，除了师父在磨刀。
他把水瓢往槽边一搁，转身回了屋。
坐在床沿上发了会儿呆，又站起来，在屋里转了两圈。
转完两圈，又坐回床沿上。
沈回想了想，觉得还是得去。
他站起身，整了整衣襟，又整了整袖口，把道袍上的褶子抻平，把腰带系紧。
走到门口，又折回来，对着墙角那只缺了口的瓦盆照了照。
头发还算整齐，脸上也没什么脏东西。
行吧，死也要死得体面些。
他深吸一口气，推门出去。
从东院到师父的静室，这条路沈回走过几回，不算长，可今天走起来却觉得特别短，短到他还没来得及做好心理建设，就已经站在了那扇门前。
门虚掩着。
里面静悄悄的，什么声音都没有。
沈回竖起耳朵听了听，没有磨刀声。难道是已经磨完了，正等着自己上门？
他咽了口唾沫，抬手，敲门。
“笃笃笃。”
“进来。”
师父的声音从里面传出来，听着好像也没什么异常。
沈回推开门。
老道士盘腿坐在蒲团上，面前的矮几上摆着一面铜镜。
铜镜旁边整整齐齐码着一排东西：剪刀，剃刀，还有一把小镊子。
沈回的脚步顿在门槛上，一时间不知道该进还是该退。
老道士抬起头看了他一眼。
那一眼平平淡淡的，看不出什么情绪，可沈回倒是觉得，老道士要是骂他两句还好，什么都不说才叫吓人。
更吓人的是师父的脸。
那张原本清瘦端正的脸上，左边眉毛全没了，右边只剩半截，像是被人拿剪刀胡乱绞过。
胡子更惨。
原本一绺漂亮的灰白长须，此刻七零八落，长短不齐，有的地方烧得只剩胡茬，有的地方干脆秃了，露出下面的下巴颏。
当然，头发也没好到哪儿去。
发髻还勉强挽着，可边缘一圈全焦了，像是被火撩过的枯草。
content_en:
Water dripped down at the feet, spreading a small patch of dark color on the bluestone.
Sharpen the knife.
The master is sharpening the knife.
Shen Hui lowered his head and looked at his hands that had just been set on fire yesterday, and then looked up at the sky.
The sun was nice, the wind was gentle, and there were two sparrows sitting on the old locust tree in the corner of the courtyard, chirping happily.
Everything was fine, except that the master was sharpening his knife.
He put the water ladle on the edge of the sink and turned back to the house.
He sat on the edge of the bed in a daze for a while, then stood up and walked around the room twice.
After turning twice, he sat back on the edge of the bed.
Shen thought about it and felt that he still had to go.
He stood up, straightened his clothes and cuffs, straightened the pleats on his robe, and tightened his belt.
He walked to the door, turned back, and took a look at the chipped pot in the corner.
His hair was fairly neat and there was nothing dirty on his face.
Okay, let's die in a dignified way.
He took a deep breath and pushed the door open.
From the east courtyard to Master's quiet room, Shen Hui walked this road several times. It was not long, but today it felt very short when walking. It was so short that he was already standing in front of the door before he had time to mentally prepare.
The door was ajar.
It was quiet inside, no sound at all.
Shen Hui pricked up his ears and listened, but there was no sound of sharpening the knife. Could it be that it has been polished and is waiting for you to come to your door?
He swallowed, raised his hand, and knocked on the door.
"Tuk-tuk-tuk."
"Come in."
The master's voice came from inside, and it didn't sound unusual.
Shen Hui opened the door.
The old Taoist priest sat cross-legged on the futon, with a bronze mirror placed on the low table in front of him.
Next to the bronze mirror were a neat row of things: scissors, razors, and a pair of small tweezers.
Shen Hui's footsteps paused on the threshold, and for a moment he didn't know whether to advance or retreat.
The old Taoist priest raised his head and glanced at him.
The look was dull and showed no emotion, but Shen Hui felt that it would be okay if the old Taoist priest scolded him a few words, but it would be scary if he didn't say anything.
What's even more frightening is Master's face.
On the face that was originally thin and straight, the eyebrows on the left side were completely gone, and only half of the eyebrows on the right side were left, as if someone had randomly twisted them with scissors.
Beards are even worse.
What was originally a beautiful long gray beard is now all in pieces, with uneven lengths. Some places are burnt to the point where only stubble is left, and some places are simply bald, exposing the chin underneath.
Of course, the hair wasn't much better.
The bun was still barely held up, but the edges were completely burnt, like dry grass that had been stirred by fire.
